comments.body:
Added branch here:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/tree/fcrepo-1821

By default it seems that authentication has to be explicitly defined. Using the jetty-console plugin I can get closer but only by adding in the jettyXml plugin jetty-console-log4j-plugin and setting up a jetty-web.xml or jetty-console.xml and passing them via command line.

java -jar target/crepo-webapp-plus-4.4.1-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar --jettyXml jetty-console.xml

or

java -jar target/crepo-webapp-plus-4.4.1-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar --jettyWebXml jetty-web.xml

Not much documentation on this plugin.

I tried to add the jetty-web.xml to the individual WEB-INF directories for each profile, but that breaks the setting up jetty for integration testing.

Jared Whiklo, here is a first draft... it runs and does authz, but needs some help in getting the right classes loaded.
https://github.com/awoods/fcrepo-jetty-security-plugin – new plugin for adding the AuthHandler to jetty, and
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/32

This is a nice piece of work Andrew Woods. Other than the error about missing system property fcrepo.audit.container with the rbacl build, I didn't seem to have any problems. What are the classes that are missing?
Jared Whiklo checking in from the December 10 Tech Call to see if there updates on this, and Unknown recalled that might be a roadblock here.

Actually, I did hit a roadblock. But Mr. Andrew Woods used his formidable skills to create the above fcrepo-jetty-security-plugin and PR/32. He makes mention of it needing help getting the right classes loaded. But I did not encounter any issues (I might have failed in testing). Perhaps Nick Ruest would like to try them, it could be another Ubuntu thing?

The spring.handlers and spring.schemas should not be necessary to define in:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-webapp-plus/pull/32/files

I would like to see them removed from this PR. I will try to give it a look soonish (immediately and/or before the New Year)

Not that I fully understand much about spring, but is this due to the multiple profiles defined in this artifact some dependencies wiping out others? If so would the Apache Maven Shade plugin help? It appears with that type of issue.

Shade may be a solution here. I had not yet determined why shade is not needed when creating:
fcrepo-webapp-4.4.1-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar
..but may be when creating:
fcrepo-webapp-plus-audit-4.4.1-SNAPSHOT-jetty-console.jar

Shade reference: https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo4-upgrade-utils/blob/master/pom.xml#L145-L171
